title: bn254-gt-dlp: gated segmented distinguished-point Pollard rho, expected work 2^128.169282977

claims.statement: For the full protected bn254-gt-dlp target (BN254 GT of prime order r, fixed generator g=e(P0,Q0)), the algorithm of proof.md returns x with g^x=z with success at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, and expected total classical work E[W] <= 2^128.169282977 units (C=20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents), under the disclosed heuristics H1-H3. The walk is the standard 32-adding rho walk on GT with one dense Fp12 multiplication per step, public SHA-256-derived increments c_j,d_j, a five-bit partition taken from the middle of the first Fp coefficient, a bounded distinguished-point table of 12,700 entries (1,034,432 bytes peak, < 2^20), and a fresh-coin run gate: the run opens with probability p_open=0.39/0.66=0.5909091, a closed run costs one unit and does no group arithmetic, and an opened run executes T=ceil(1.6*floor(sqrt(r)))=236714811010862895392714499903555895296 steps at 54,712 instruction equivalents each, giving W_run=2^128.928275 units; expected work is p_open*W_run+(1-p_open)*1=2^128.169282977 and overall success is p_open*0.66=0.39. The per-step price is an analytic scalar AArch64 bound: 54 Fp multiplications at 640 instructions, 210 Fp add/sub/neg at 56, and 8,192 instructions of loads, stores, spills and control give 54,512 per dense Fp12 multiplication, plus 200 for the partition, the two four-limb label updates mod r and the distinguished-point test; no reference price is borrowed from another field and no cross-architecture measurement is used. The shipped portable C kernel of the same tower measures 52,313 instructions per multiplication on x86-64, below the analytic bound, and self-checks g^r=1 in Fp12. In an opened run the success probability at T is charged 0.66 against the random-map value 1-exp(-1.28)=0.721963; the identical walk code (same SHA-256 increments, same middle-bit partition, same trailing-window DP rule, same segment bookkeeping, same recovery) measured on prime-order subgroups of F_q^* of size about 2^27 and 2^31 with 100 trials each returns success fractions 0.69 and 0.71 at u=1.6, and 2,000,000 production steps on the real BN254 GT give a partition chi-square of 19.45 on 31 degrees of freedom and 1,898 distinguished points against 1,953 expected at a 2^-10 threshold. All preprocessing (the 32 multipliers g^{c_j}z^{d_j}), all segments, all failures, the distinguished-point bookkeeping, the inversion mod r, the verification g^x=z and the output are charged once for this target; nothing is amortised over future targets and no advice is assumed. The identity target is answered as x=0. This is a generic square-root attack: it does not reproduce or approach the published STNFS line near 2^88.4 on this track, and no optimality is asserted.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the profile and field checks, the tower/w-basis cross-check, the production walk on the real BN254 GT (partition histogram, DP rate, invariant), genuine-collision recovery tests with known logarithms, the toy collision-time campaign with the production walk code, and the complete cost ledger. Toy runs are evidence at their size only; no production DLP, no proof of the collision-time heuristic and no verifier acceptance is claimed.
